summary: newtun ships remote-controlled PTY backdoor to hardcoded WebSocket server
details: newtun@1.0.0 connects to a hardcoded default WebSocket control server at ws://pull.7ii.win:7999 and, on receipt of TERM_OPEN/TERM_INPUT messages, spawns an interactive PTY shell (bash on Unix, cmd.exe on Windows) and writes base64-decoded message payloads from the remote endpoint into that shell, streaming shell output back over the same socket. The remote server therefore has full interactive shell control on any host running the client. The control channel is plain ws:// with no TLS, so the auth token and all shell I/O traverse an unencrypted channel and are additionally exposed to on-path attackers. The default endpoint is not a caller-configured destination; installing and running this package yields remote code execution on the host by whoever controls pull.7ii.win.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
